title: Roham Gharegozlou | The Past, Present, and Future of Crypto | Talks at Google
description:
Roham Gharegozlou discusses his company Dapper Labs, the detailed history of cryptocurrency and where he sees it going in the near future.

Roham Gharegozlou is the co-founder and CEO of Dapper Labs and a leader in blockchain and Web3 technology. He is often cited as the pioneer of NFTs, with CryptoKitties being the first viral NFT project that broke Ethereum in 2017. From those learnings, Roham launched Dapper Labs from Axiom Zen in 2018, aiming to drive mainstream adoption of decentralized technologies and put a crypto wallet in every pocket. Today, Dapper Labs has made Web3 accessible for developers, creators, and users by designing Flow, a decentralized Web3 platform built for consumer-friendly dApps that now has more than 3.6 million accounts; releasing Dapper Wallet, the easiest way to get started on Web3; and launching dApps, including NBA Top Shot (with more than 1.3M community members and nearly $1B in sales), UFC Strike, NFL ALL DAY, Seussibles, and more that are attracting millions to Web3.

For more information on Dapper Labs, please visit https://www.dapperlabs.com/.

Moderated by David Lawee.

David Lawee founded CapitalG, Alphabet's independent growth fund, in 2013, drawing on his experience at Google and as a serial entrepreneur. Since then, he has helped transform high-potential startups into some of the most highly-valued businesses of our generation, including Airbnb, Lyft, Snap, Robinhood, Credit Karma, Niantic, Digital Currency Group, and Fireblocks. Previously, David played a pivotal role in Google’s growth story, first as Google’s CMO and then as the company’s first VP of corporate development where his team led more than 100 acquisitions for the company. Before joining Google, David successfully founded a number of startup ventures including Xfire, a leading online gaming community acquired by Viacom, and Mosaic Venture Partners, a Toronto-based venture capital firm.

For more information on CapitalG please visit https://capitalg.com/.

#talk
summary: The speaker argues that large technology companies like Google, Netflix, Amazon, and Microsoft are currently struggling to find a relevant role in legitimizing the crypto space. He suggests that while Google Cloud could be a strong infrastructure partner for the Flow platform, the broader market has shown that no asset class, including major tech stocks, has been immune to significant volatility. Ultimately, the talk questions the current ability of these established giants to meaningfully integrate with or support the crypto ecosystem.

numbers.what: size of the Flow Fund
numbers.quote: I know you've started-- you have been a participant, I guess, in the blockchain-- in the Flow Fund, $750 million Flow Fund.

numbers.what: amount of investment per company by Dapper Labs
numbers.quote: We're very small amounts, usually from $25,000 to $100,000, some $1 million, more, but very small amounts.

numbers.what: total capital raised by invested companies
numbers.quote: Those companies have gone on to raise over $3 billion from other venture capitalists, you know, Andreessen, COTU, Tiger, Sequoia, all of these folks.

numbers.what: total value of the Flow Fund
numbers.quote: And the $750 million fund isn't our dollars. It's actually primarily from folks like Andreessen, and COTU, and USV, Venrock, CoinFund, whatever it might be. And so we've-- as Dapper Labs, we've seen all these folks splashing this money around. And we've seen, well, we have-- we've got cash in the bank. We could be splashing money. We could be selling tokens. But hey, I'd rather keep the tokens for the long term, and use the cash to build products that create more cash, and then get the VCs to invest in the next generation of products on top of our platforms. But we're going to get a transaction fee. We're going to get the sort of token appreciation value, et cetera. And that's the perspective we've taken is let professionals allocate capital to the best companies rather than have companies just come to us because we're handing out-- we're handing out cash and incentives. And so that's largely been the perspective we've taken with the capital. And the ecosystem is pretty well-funded, you know, $3.5 billion or so, mostly raised pretty recently. And that $750 million is over $1 billion now.
